subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw expose this as a local web_fetch/web_search config policy, route it through managed proxy policy, or require a broader cross-tool egress contract first?
rationale: This is a public operator-trusted security boundary, and the existing open PRs choose different boundaries that automation should not settle without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Use the open hostname-allowlist PR as an incremental first step while keeping deny domains, managed search, and proxy coverage tracked on this issue.

options.title: Make managed proxy policy canonical
options.body: Pause local web_fetch config expansion and make operator-managed proxy policy the egress boundary for app-owned web traffic.

options.title: Require cross-tool design first
options.body: Hold implementation until maintainers define one policy across fetch, search, browser navigation, redirects, caches, provider fallback, and plugin HTTP.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Use the open hostname-allowlist PR as an incremental first step while keeping deny domains, managed search, and proxy coverage tracked on this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent web_fetch and SSRF-policy history and owns the closest open allowlist implementation path.
